doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Stephanie Trick and the James P. Johnson project
summary: Her multimedia shows and album with Stephanie Trick, and what makes a good accompanist.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. The collaboration you did with Stephanie Trick was pretty amazing. Is there any plans for more of that?

Well no, not right now. And I miss Stephanie a great deal. Performing with her was just fantastic. We had a multi-media thing going that her late father had put together with lyrics on a screen and then there’s a little cam on Stephanie’s flying fingers. And we had a video and various pictures of James P. Johnson, Fats Waller. But that was a moment in time. We just became fans of each other through mutual friends and we got together — © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

we thought it would be good to do a gig and then we said well let’s do an album. And I had used up so many Fats Waller tunes on my own Fats album that we tried to concentrate on James P. Johnson. But Stephanie, who was — I always forget how old she is — but she looked like she was 12 at the time I was working with her, she was so young. But she knew all of this old James P. Johnson stuff and Willie “The Lion” Smith and some other composers I’d never heard of. There was a guy named Robin Frost who wrote something called — I think it was Robin Frost — “Greased Limelight” that, it was written to be played by computer because it was pretty much unplayable. But Stephanie played it. And I wrote lyrics to it and called it, “Let’s Do This.” So she was just this amazing trove of information about music — I mean Fats Waller died before even I was born and Stephanie just — she was just created to do this. So we did the album and we did some gigs together that were super fun. I would say it was maybe the most entertaining musical performance I’ve ever been part of. And her husband, Paolo, is a an — Alderighi — is a fantastic player, and then they would do a thing together. It was just like huge fun. It’s very hard to remember all those lyrics. I really don’t drink at all anymore but at the time I did, but never before that show. Because it’s intense remembering all of it. But yeah, I’m just crazy about her and I would like to work with her again, perform with her again.
Wow. That’s sort of a specialized genre but over the years can you articulate what makes for a valuable piano accompanist?

Well because I do songs that were already arranged by the composers it’s not necessarily an issue because the usual answer to that would be someone who doesn’t overplay, someone who doesn’t rush. But I play, have performed almost exclusively with the guys who wrote the music. So it just doesn’t come up. With Russell, with Shelly and with Stephanie of course. So it’s completely natural. It’s difficult to do it with another person. Songs that I might not think are terribly difficult somebody, I tried to do them with players that everyone said oh this is the best guy in such-and-such town. And it would be someone who is great but he’d go like, “This song is just almost impossible to pull off I don’t know if I can do it.” So it’s kind of challenging.
